metadata.title: Fine tuning the glycolytic flux ratio of EP-bifido pathway for mevalonate production by enhancing glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (Zwf) and CRISPRi suppressing 6-phosphofructose kinase (PfkA) in Escherichia coli

reference.title: Fine tuning the glycolytic flux ratio of EP-bifido pathway for mevalonate production by enhancing glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (Zwf) and CRISPRi suppressing 6-phosphofructose kinase (PfkA) in Escherichia coli

target.condition: 50-mL shake flasks, M9 + 0.2% yeast extract + 20 g/L glucose, 37 °C, 120 rpm; MVA titers reported at 72 h (Methods state 48 h - inconsistency)

trigger.observation: Prior 13C-MFA of the EP-bifido MVA strain showed PPP split ratio too low (0.43:0.57 EMP:PPP vs theoretical optimum 1:6) with insufficient NADPH from oxidative PPP.
trigger.reasoning: Enhance PPP flux and NADPH supply by replacing the genomic zwf promoter with graded-strength constitutive promoters, and test effect on MVA production
trigger.source_location: BW-P (BW25113 ΔpfkA::FRT) derivatives BW-P 23100/23104/23105/23108/23114-zwf, each carrying pBSA + pFF (BW-P10/04/05/08/14 BF)

evidence.source_location: BW-P BF (BW-P/pBSA pFF, native zwf promoter)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Trigger and outcome are measured: prior 13C-MFA split ratio, fermentation titers, and this study's 13C-MFA showing increased oxidative PPP flux and promoter-strength-correlated NADPH.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: genomic zwf promoter replacement via Red homologous recombination (CmR cassette, 300-500 bp homology arms); transformation with MVA pathway plasmids pBSA (atoB, mvaS, mvaA) and pFF (fbp, fxpk)

result.metric: MVA titer and molar conversion rate (HPLC), OD600, glucose consumption over fermentation
result.after: BW-P10 BF (J23100): 11.2 g/L MVA, 62.2% conversion at 72 h; BBa-J23100 and BBa-J23108 gave highest yields (64.3% and 62.3% mol/mol per Results text); growth and glucose consumption similar to control; fewer byproducts

decision_chain.rule: When an acetyl-CoA-derived, NADPH-dependent product (e.g., mevalonate in an E. coli EP-bifido system) is limited by an EMP/PPP split skewed toward EMP, apply graded-strength promoter replacement at the zwf locus, because increasing G6PDH flux stoichiometrically raises NADPH supply - while noting yield does not scale monotonically with promoter strength, so a promoter ladder rather than the single strongest promoter should be screened.

target.condition: same shake-flask fermentation regime as EXP2; induction at 12 h

trigger.observation: The static pfkA knockout in the EP-bifido strain caused severe growth defects, limiting applicability; early-growth carbon should ideally go to biomass, so flexible/timed repression was needed.
trigger.reasoning: Replace the static, growth-damaging pfkA knockout with time-controlled, tunable CRISPRi repression to dynamically balance EMP/PPP flux and improve MVA conversion
trigger.source_location: BW25113 23100-zwf (pfkA intact, zwf promoter replaced with BBa-J23100) carrying CRISPRi plasmid combinations: pBSA-dCas9+pFF-sgRNA1/2/3 (BiBF1-3) or pBSA-sgRNA1/2/3+pFF-dCas9 (BiB1F/BiB2F/BiB3F)

evidence.source_location: BBF (BW25113 23100-zwf + pFF + pBSA, no CRISPRi); additional component controls BB1F, BBFd, BiBd1F (EXP5, Figure S1)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Fermentation outcomes (growth, glucose, MVA titer/yield, byproducts) were measured for all six CRISPRi strains and four component controls.

alternatives.approach: Promoter-replacement methods for down-regulation (rejected: CRISPRi does not require genome editing of the target gene)
Post-transcriptional/post-translational tools such as anti-sense RNA and RNAi (mentioned as alternatives, not tested)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: CRISPRi system: dcas9 under weak promoter BBa-J23134; three sgRNAs targeting pfkA promoter region (sgRNA1), +100 bp (sgRNA2) and +200 bp (sgRNA3) downstream of start codon; IPTG-inducible expression, induced with 200 µM IPTG at 12 h

result.metric: MVA titer/yield (HPLC), OD600, glucose consumption, byproduct (acetate/ethanol) detection
result.after: sgRNA1 (promoter-targeting) gave best repression balance; BiB1F reached 8.53 g/L MVA and 68.7% molar conversion - highest reported shake-flask MVA conversion; CRISPRi introduction reduced growth and glucose consumption (attributed to dCas9 toxicity/leaky expression); acetate/ethanol byproducts hardly detected

decision_chain.rule: When a competing-glycolytic-pathway knockout (e.g., pfkA) improves product yield but causes severe growth defects in an E. coli acetyl-CoA-derived production system, apply inducible CRISPRi repression targeting the gene's promoter region with a weakly expressed dCas9, because tunable, time-delayed transcriptional repression preserves early-growth EMP flux while still redirecting carbon toward the product pathway after induction.

rule_provenance.rule: When an acetyl-CoA-derived, NADPH-dependent product (e.g., mevalonate in an E. coli EP-bifido system) is limited by an EMP/PPP split skewed toward EMP, apply graded-strength promoter replacement at the zwf locus, because increasing G6PDH flux stoichiometrically raises NADPH supply - while noting yield does not scale monotonically with promoter strength, so a promoter ladder rather than the single strongest promoter should be screened.

When a competing-glycolytic-pathway knockout (e.g., pfkA) improves product yield but causes severe growth defects in an E. coli acetyl-CoA-derived production system, apply inducible CRISPRi repression targeting the gene's promoter region with a weakly expressed dCas9, because tunable, time-delayed transcriptional repression preserves early-growth EMP flux while still redirecting carbon toward the product pathway after induction.
